summary: CR-001 is corrected: reporting and verification use cash_obligation.amount_minor; the UI preserves zero remainders and falls back to the total when payment is null. Zero cash can be reported and verified. CR-003 protects newly approved documents from upload-ticket overwrites. Row locking, UUID-derived document keys and the private_key UNIQUE constraint introduce no identified collision regression; successful writes receive rollback cleanup, re-completion returns the approved asset, and deletion targets the sealed key. One cleanup failure remains below. CR-002 is not established as a code defect: docs/product/06-permissions.md:26 assigns staff-session MFA enforcement to the identity provider, while StaffAssurance enforces recent MFA on selected high-risk actions. Password-only test authentication does not demonstrate a production provider-policy bypass. Provider MFA configuration still needs deployment evidence. Review was static; integration tests were not run and report files were not written because the sandbox is read-only.

commands.note: Reviewed all five changed files and related storage, payment, authorization and migration code.

findings.title: Upload cleanup failure cannot be recovered by re-completion
findings.scenario: Sealing and database commit succeed, but deleting uploads/<id> fails with a transient S3 error in the afterCommit callback.
findings.expected: Approval remains successfully observable and failed cleanup is durably retried, including when the owner later deletes the document.
findings.actual: The callback exception escapes after approval has committed. Re-completion returns immediately for APPROVED media without retrying cleanup. The row now stores only documents/<id>, so the delete path also leaves the original upload object behind.
findings.evidence: Line 210 schedules an unguarded storage.delete; afterCommit executes action.run() at line 297. S3ObjectStorage.delete propagates SDK failures. Completion returns early at lines 132-133, and delete removes only row.privateKey() at line 242. No durable cleanup retry is registered.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist an idempotent cleanup job transactionally with approval and retry storage deletion independently. Prevent cleanup failures from turning committed approval into an error response.
findings.repro_test: Inject a one-time failure deleting uploads/<id>. Complete a synthetic document, retry completion, then delete it. Assert approval remains successful and a durable retry eventually removes the upload object. Not executed.
